title: AI agent firm Instinct raises $1 billion in latest funding round
gist: AI personal-assistant startup Instinct raised a $1B Series C at a $10B valuation from Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue, 4x its valuation from a month earlier, despite disclosing no user or growth figures and facing competition from Meta's Muse.

insights.claim: Instinct raised $1 billion in a Series C at a $10 billion valuation with Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital and Coatue participating.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Top-tier VCs are paying up for consumer action-taking AI agents.
insights.locator: AI agent startup Instinct said Monday

insights.claim: Instinct's $10 billion valuation is four times the $2.5 billion attached to its $250 million raise reported just a month earlier.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A 4x step-up in a month signals frothy private-market pricing for AI agents.
insights.quote: The valuation is four times the $2.5 billion figure attached to Instinct’s previous $250 million raise, reported just last month.

insights.claim: Instinct has not disclosed user totals or growth figures, leaving outsiders little basis to judge how its valuation relates to adoption or revenue.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Valuation is running ahead of disclosed fundamentals, a bubble-risk marker.
insights.quote: the company has not disclosed user totals or growth figures

insights.claim: The rapid funding reflects investor interest in AI agents that take actions on a user's behalf rather than simply answer questions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Capital is rotating from chat to action-taking agents.

insights.claim: Instinct faces a crowded market including Meta's Muse, which offers similar assistance and connects to Meta's social platforms that already reach millions of users.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Distribution-rich incumbents threaten standalone agent startups.
insights.locator: Instinct is entering a more crowded market.

insights.claim: Agents completing purchases, schedules and messages need sensitive personal data, so trust and error detection may matter as much as convenience; Instinct says it is improving privacy safeguards and error detection.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Privacy and reliability failures are a key adoption risk for consumer agents.
insights.quote: Trust may prove just as important as convenience.
insights.locator: Trust may prove just as important

insights.claim: Founded in 2025 by Noah Shinn, Instinct's invite-only assistant handles errands via text or phone, and a newer concierge feature calls businesses to book appointments and reservations.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Voice-calling agents that interact with businesses are a live product category.
